## F-R05 — Canonical decision text is the secondary ordering key

L-O22 and F-R01 require retained decisions sorted by event reference, then by the canonical JSON text of the decision itself. The unaccepted generated candidate bound below instead uses the canonical JSON text of the containing {event, obstruction} record as its secondary key. Whole-record ordering is not equivalent when one decision encoding is a prefix of another: the surrounding punctuation affects comparison. Canonical record identity remains useful for validation but must not substitute for the specified comparison dimension.

Perform an isolated exact-substring source-patchset codemod on `src/semiotic-eavt/journal/substrate.mjs` in the bound staged candidate root. Its input SHA-256 is `6695957bf6ac70b25095a48072bd7760081d120481fafdf197840da74c6e262f`. Change only the internal secondary comparison-key construction so it is the exact canonical text of the already snapshotted obstruction value, using the existing imported canonicalizeJson and JSON_RESOURCE_ENVELOPE. The record returned to callers remains the exact immutable event/obstruction snapshot. Preserve event-first comparison, exact-decision deduplication, collection validation, blocking and reception rules, snapshots and exports. Do not rewrite the surrounding module or change its host boundary.

The staged candidate is migration input, not an accepted implementation. All L-O22/F-R01–F-R04 requirements still govern the composed candidate. Use the existing source-patchset edit representation and isolated GPT-6 Luna provider, with no checkout or private receiving data. Before invocation, commit independent receiving for the whole composed behavior, including exact decision-order semantics. Recheck all read-only inputs and the original repository source before any promotion. Root materialization remains mechanical; no hand repair is authorized. Acceptance of the corrected pure reconstruction remains separate from source-owner integration and the complete assistant workflow.

title: Preserve retained admission decisions during causal reconstruction
date-created: 2026-09-27

Realize L-O22 through the existing F-P01–F-P06 source-patchset contract and L-F01–L-F07 isolation and independent receiving. The useful effect is preservation of historically blocked events and their blocked descendants when rebuilding from retained sources. Extend the existing Code causal substrate; do not create a second reconstruction service or move pure causal judgment into Systems. This dependency is required by the shared journal owner. Its acceptance alone does not establish a usable journal or assistant.

## F-R01 — Exact writable scope and input boundary

The only writable file is `src/semiotic-eavt/journal/substrate.mjs` under the existing Code section, with original SHA-256 `bbeaf4c9a918f0e16787b461c46aefe46458aa31d47fbacfe8d8586d3151b84c`. Submit an edit patchset with exact-substring replacements; source creation, deletion and changes to other modules are refused. Preserve the existing exports evaluateWitnessDependencies, CausalSubstrate, createCausalSubstrate and rebuildCausalSubstrate. No new public export or package export is needed. Preserve existing constructor/create entrypoint signatures; an internal initializer may carry validated historical decisions for rebuild without exposing a new admission operation.

Extend rebuildCausalSubstrate with L-O22's optional fourth argument. Before creating/exposing any new source view, validate the retainedObstructions collection as an ordinary dense Array whose own keys are exactly length and contiguous indices, with only data descriptors. Refuse symbols, extra properties, sparse entries, accessors and exotic array prototypes without invoking property accessors. Validate collection shape in linear work in its own-key count: use one own-key set or one key pass plus descriptor checks, not repeated whole-key-array scans for each index. Own numeric data properties may be nonenumerable; enumerability is not part of the collection law. Each index must still be present and a data descriptor. Snapshot each `{event, obstruction}` entry through canonicalizeJson with JSON_RESOURCE_ENVELOPE, then check its exact keys and event through isArtifactRef. This preserves falsy decisions, rejects unsupported JSON and bounds each entry. Sort by event and canonical decision text; omit only canonical duplicates. Do not collapse different decisions for one event. Return L-O22's fixed retained-obstruction-invalid judgment for validation failures. Do not use JSON.stringify on unchecked input or call user getters/toJSON. Collection bounds are the host's already specified source limits, not a new arbitrary low array-length cap.

## F-R02 — Blocking before promotion

Seed the validated immutable historical decision set before any artifact reception or promotion. Historical membership takes precedence in witnessState; a matching core is never added to the quarantined or admitted sets. Both receive and receiveSourceSet must preserve this condition when a formerly absent body arrives. Keep the existing cause-blocked dependency rule, so transitive descendants cannot be promoted. Reuse existing graph-cycle and artifact/core validation. Missing historical body does not create an artifact or core. The fixed retained-block explanation is a derived causal judgment, while every raw historical decision remains separately recoverable.

Retain the original missing-dependency recovery behavior for unrelated unblocked witnesses. An eligible independent witness remains admitted; an unrelated pending witness can become admitted on later source arrival. Three-argument rebuild calls and ordinary receive calls retain their established behavior. A validation failure must not expose a partially built reconstruction or modify caller input. No API adds or removes historical decisions from an existing instance; the host refresh supplies the complete decision set when reconstructing a new logical view.

## F-R03 — Recoverable outputs and purity

Implement retainedObstructions() and the snapshot retainedObstructions field exactly as L-O22. Return deeply immutable canonical snapshots, sorted and deduplicated without changing the original decision's JSON meaning. sourceArtifacts remains actual verified source bodies only; witness lists contain actual cores only; blocked lists include historically blocked references even without a core. Keep other existing snapshot and reception fields and semantics. Do not export host diagnostics, invent an admitted flag, persist a block index, or create a mutable unblocking operation.

Existing direct imports remain allowed: ../identity/index.mjs, ./judgment.mjs, ./causal-graph.mjs and ./witness.mjs. The only additional allowed direct import is @red-cup-engineering/json-services-section for canonicalizeJson and JSON_RESOURCE_ENVELOPE. isArtifactRef is available from the existing identity import. No new dependency installation, filesystem/network/process/environment access, dynamic import, eval or Function construction is authorized. Read-only transitive dependencies must be resolved and content-bound before generation.

## F-R04 — Independent receiving and promotion

Bind this order, L-O22, the exact original module, its read-only API dependencies, the source-patchset schema and a private receiving commitment before the isolated requested GPT-6 Luna call. The public input contains no private fixtures or previous private feedback. Materialize only the declared edit mechanically. Syntax-check the receiving program before its commitment so a fixture infrastructure error cannot be mistaken for candidate failure. Run the candidate with actual artifact/journal primitives in a network-denied namespace.

Independent observations must exercise: a complete blocked cause plus descendant; source and decision permutations; duplicate and differing decisions; absent blocked body followed by receive and receiveSourceSet; a longer descendant chain; unrelated eligible and recoverable pending witnesses; unchanged no-history reconstruction; null/false/zero/string/object decisions; immutable snapshots detached from caller mutation; reconstruction from sourceArtifacts plus retainedObstructions; invalid reference/shape/accessor/sparse collection refusal; and no manufactured source for a bodyless historical block. Review the changed source for hidden host effects and changes outside the selected causal rule. Recheck the exact original source and all bound inputs before promotion. A refused candidate is not hand-repaired or silently regenerated from private failure details. Record the concrete observed effects and limitations, not a general journal or application success claim.

## What this is

This LLD closes H-F2/H-F3's first source-derivation realization using existing inference and isolation tools, without adding a scheduler, gateway, generator framework, or application-specific fabricator. It governs an operator-mediated transformation from a closed fabrication order into a staged candidate and separately held acceptance evidence. It is a bounded first realization, not automation of the whole Customer Demand-to-code chain.

## Work-order and candidate carriers

**L-F01.** The admitted generation input MUST bind the predecessor chain, fabrication order, current transformation-input bytes/digests, public examples, output contract, model/configuration and invocation bounds. The input MUST exclude private assay source, fixtures, expected results and assessor conversation. A separate assessor MUST derive and commit the private assay inventory before source derivation starts. Commitment is a byte digest, not proof that the assay is sufficient.

**L-F02.** The first output contract is a closed JSON object with `disposition` (`candidate` or `refused`), `reason`, and `edits`. A refused result MUST have no edits and a specific reason. Each candidate edit MUST contain exactly `path`, `inputSha256`, `before`, `after`, and `clauses`. `path` identifies an admitted relative source file, `inputSha256` binds its original bytes, `before` is a nonempty exact substring occurring once at the point of application, `after` is replacement text, and `clauses` is a nonempty array of governing clause IDs. Multiple edits to a file apply in output order against one original input digest. Missing files, ambiguous text matches, path escape, mismatched input digest, unrecognized clause IDs, or extra object fields MUST refuse materialization. Candidate outputs are untrusted source until independently assessed.

The deterministic materializer applies only admitted textual replacements to a staged copy and computes full resulting file digests. This is a bounded codemod application, not behavioral source derivation. It MUST NOT execute generator-provided shell commands. New files require a separately specified creation contract; this first work order uses existing files. Actual transformed bytes, input/output digests and clause correspondence become the source-result evidence required by H-F2/F-H07.

## Generator access boundary

**L-F03.** The source provider MUST run in a fresh inference context with no inherited conversation, no assessor material, and no shared-checkout write access. For the first local realization, the existing Codex executable MAY be invoked noninteractively with the requested GPT-6 Luna model inside a Bubblewrap mount/PID namespace. The only task content is the public input packet delivered on standard input. The host checkout, assay directory, host process namespace, session history, user/project configuration, skills and connectors MUST NOT be mounted or otherwise supplied. The public output schema MAY be mounted read-only. Runtime libraries, TLS/DNS files and the existing authentication file may be made available solely to run the authenticated provider; authentication material MUST NOT be printed or placed in prompts.

The invocation MUST use a fresh ephemeral session, ignore user configuration and rules, disable shell, web search, apps and further agent delegation where the installed CLI supports those controls, and use a read-only model-command sandbox. External process isolation supplies the filesystem boundary; prompts and the CLI's read-only setting alone do not. Native tools which remain advertised cannot see the omitted mounts. The invocation MUST NOT resume this conversation or any previous source/assessor session. The actual argument vector, executable digest/version, public input digest, observed model and event record MUST be retained without credentials. Undeclared tool use, unexpected mounts, source input change, unavailable authentication/model, or source-provider access to assessor material MUST reject that invocation. No alternate model is silently substituted.

**L-F04.** Before live source generation, a deterministic process under the same mount profile MUST establish that the host checkout and an external sentinel cannot be read, that the process view is namespaced, and that only the intended task inputs are available. This demonstrates the local process boundary, not provider-server confidentiality or model correctness. The provider's own server retention/isolation remains a trust assumption and MUST be stated. The operator MUST NOT send private assay content through feedback, diagnostics or a resumed source session.

## Independent assessment and promotion

**L-F05.** The assessor MUST run the committed assays against the content-bound candidate, separately from the source provider. Executing candidate code MUST not give it a communication channel back to that provider or access to operational credentials/private user data. A network-denied execution namespace with only required runtime, dependency, candidate and assay inputs is the selected local assessment boundary. The assessor may inspect private results; the source generator receives only a separately admitted public reproduction or changed specification, never private fixtures or raw assay logs.

**L-F06.** The evidence bundle MUST contain specification/chain/input/candidate/assay digests, provider/model/configuration, invocation boundaries, method, environment, assessor, result, limits, and measured token/time/cost information where available. Missing cash-cost data MUST be marked unavailable rather than zero. Generic artifact receipts may reference this bundle by locator/digest; receipts do not prove acceptance. Failed candidates remain rejected. New evidence or revised specifications can justify a new candidate; an invisible edit after a failed assay cannot.

**L-F07.** Promotion MUST compare each original input digest with current shared-checkout bytes immediately before applying the accepted replacements. Any mismatch refuses the entire promotion batch and preserves both candidate and concurrent edits. All affected files must pass this check before any is replaced. Promotion MUST retain the accepted output digest and actual receiving-workflow evidence; staging checks do not establish public deployment or assistant operation.

## Implementations

The installed host currently has Bubblewrap and Codex CLI 0.154.0. A preliminary empty namespace probe could not see `/home/emsenn/info`; the complete invocation profile still requires L-F04's recorded check. The CLI's local help exposes ephemeral, ignored-user-config, output-schema and noninteractive execution. [Official configuration documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/config-reference) defines the shell-tool switch; [noninteractive documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/non-interactive-mode) describes the ephemeral invocation. These are invocation capabilities, not proof of assay independence or generated-code correctness.

The separately inspected ops inference route reported one configured `llama3.2:3b` provider with no admitted resource-availability observation. It was not invoked or substituted for the requested Luna source role. Its existence is not evidence of available capacity. The local invocation above uses existing tooling; no inference service is being repaired or reimplemented here.

## Open questions

- **L-FO1:** The first source invocation must establish actual model/authentication availability and record L-F04's complete boundary check. Failure preserves the closed order and assays; it does not authorize direct hand coding.
- **L-FO2:** Broader unattended generation, scheduler integration and automatic demand-to-design derivation are not supplied by this operator-mediated protocol. Any subsequent automation must preserve these contracts and receive its own specification before implementation.

## Necessary transformation

L-F02's exact-substring contract cannot create a System module or retire its superseded Code implementation. L-S06/L-S09 require both effects, including consumer migration. This order extends the deterministic materialization boundary for explicitly declared source creation and deletion. It does not add a scheduler, model harness, repository mutation service or product-code generator. Existing edit-only orders and their evidence remain unchanged. The source provider continues deriving behavioral source; the operator's deterministic materializer performs only declared byte transformations on a fresh staged directory.

**F-P01 — Opt-in input.** A patchset work order binds an exact source root and an input inventory. The inventory is a JSON object with exactly `kind`, `version`, `sourceRoot`, `files`, `clauses`. Kind is `source-patchset-input`; version is integer 1. SourceRoot is an absolute existing directory. Files is a path-keyed object. Every key is an admitted relative POSIX source path: nonempty components, each matching `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+`, no dot/dot-dot component, absolute prefix, backslash or NUL. Each descriptor is exactly either `{state:"present",sha256}` or `{state:"absent"}`. Present entries bind lowercase SHA-256 of original bytes; absent entries authorize only creation. No path may be an ancestor of another admitted path. Clauses is a nonempty unique list of recognized nonempty clause-ID strings. Existing paths must be ordinary regular files and all existing ancestors, including the root's own path, must be nonsymlink directories; absent paths must also have no symlink or nondirectory ancestor. The inventory is trusted work-order input, not generated permission to touch files.

The concrete storage order must enumerate its exact writable files and clause IDs before source generation. This generic extension grants no writable source path by itself. Read-only dependencies and governing specification hashes remain protected under L-F01/L-F07 and are additional to this writable inventory.

**F-P02 — Closed candidate.** The new opt-in output is exactly `{kind:"source-patchset",version:1,disposition,reason,changes}`. Disposition is `candidate` or `refused`; reason is a string. A refusal has zero changes. A candidate has at least one change. Each admitted path occurs at most once, and every change contains a nonempty unique `clauses` array drawn from the inventory. No generated shell command, URL, dependency installation, permission change or recursive delete operation exists.

Changes are exactly one of:

- `{operation:"edit",path,inputSha256,replacements,clauses}` against a present entry. Each replacement is exactly `{before,after}`. Before is nonempty text occurring exactly once when that replacement is applied; after is text. Apply replacements in order against the original bound UTF-8 text. The one input digest remains the original file digest, not an intermediate value. The list is nonempty.
- `{operation:"create",path,text,clauses}` against an absent entry. Text is complete strict UTF-8 source, supplied by the generator; the operator must not fill behavioral placeholders. Creation emits an ordinary file with mode 0644. An executable entrypoint should normally be invoked through its existing runtime; changing execution bits requires a separately admitted order.
- `{operation:"delete",path,inputSha256,clauses}` against a present entry. This removes that exact file from the staged result. It does not delete directories, follow links, delete imports automatically or authorize removing unlisted data. Necessary consumer and export changes must appear as separately bound changes in the same work family.

All objects are closed. Reject Boolean values masquerading as integer versions, unknown operations, malformed digests, repeated paths, unknown clauses, invalid UTF-8, missing inputs, changed input bytes or an unexpectedly present creation target. Do not normalize generated paths or repair a refused candidate.

**F-P03 — Validate before staging.** The materializer rechecks every inventory entry, including unchanged inputs, before creating any staged output. It validates the whole candidate and calculates all intended output bytes in memory before writing. A malformed candidate therefore leaves no stage directory. It may inspect file metadata and bytes, but it never imports, evaluates or executes candidate text. The only mechanical transformations are the specified text replacements, creation and file omission.

Use a fresh nonexistent stage directory outside the source root. A stage ancestor cannot be a symlink or non-directory. The operator chooses that path; it is not accepted from the candidate. Copy each unchanged admitted present file and each resulting changed file into the stage at its declared relative path, preserving the existing file's permission bits for retained/edited files. Deleted inputs are omitted and their digests/modes retained in the receipt. Do not copy the repository's unbounded contents or leave links from the stage into the working checkout. Recheck all original inputs after staging before writing the staged result receipt. A concurrent change invalidates the stage and prevents acceptance; it does not authorize changing the concurrent work.

A host I/O error during staging may leave a partial staged directory. It must have no successful receipt; report failure and preserve it for inspection. Do not represent staging as an atomic multi-file filesystem transaction. A retry uses a fresh stage and fresh validation rather than overwriting an uncertain directory.

**F-P04 — Staged receipt and assessment.** The operator writes a sibling `<stage>.receipt.json` only after successful validation/staging/revalidation. The receipt contains kind `source-patchset-stage`, integer version 1, inventory/candidate digests, the materializer digest, each original path's presence/digest/mode, each final path's presence/digest/mode, and disposition `staged-unaccepted`. No receipt claims product acceptance or promotion. A receipt target already present refuses before staging; receipt creation is exclusive. A receipt write failure is a failed stage operation even if all source files have been written.

Independent assessment uses the exact staged tree plus explicitly admitted read-only dependencies. A retired file must be absent from that assessment namespace; a fallback mount of the old checkout must not make deleted code available again. Verify source creation, changed consumers and actual retired routes, not only that new files load. The private assessment remains excluded from source generation under L-F03–L-F05. Source provider and materializer receive no permission to amend acceptance fixtures after a failure.

**F-P05 — Promotion remains separate.** This materializer has no shared-checkout mutation or deployment mode. Product promotion remains governed by L-F07 plus the concrete work order's creation/deletion preconditions. Recheck all present/absent expectations before touching any target. Do not delete an obsolete file unless the complete affected capability and consumer migration have independently passed. A staged tree, deleted-path list or model assertion is insufficient. A multi-file promotion must record partial host failure accurately; it must not claim atomicity that the filesystem mechanism does not provide. Never restore over unrelated concurrent edits while trying to roll back a partial operation.

**F-P06 — Independent mechanical observations.** Demonstrate in disposable files that one batch creates a new file, changes an exact unique substring, retires a bound old file and carries an unchanged input, while leaving the source root byte-identical. Exercise stale/absent mismatch, ambiguous replacement, malformed/extra fields, repeated changes, unknown clause, path traversal, symlink input/ancestor, a path ancestor collision, malformed UTF-8 and an existing stage/receipt. Invalid input must produce no successful receipt or shared source mutation. The observations verify deterministic materialization only; they do not accept any journal or assistant behavior.

The initial realization may be a small operator-owned script retained with the fabrication evidence and invoked directly. It is not a new runtime package. This is mechanical tooling under the closed contract above; all product behavioral text in real candidates must still originate from the admitted isolated source-generation process.

## L-O22 — Historical blocking in the Code reconstruction law

Derive this refinement from L-S01's retained decisions and L-S05's common source-derived state. The current `rebuildCausalSubstrate(sources, site, causalEnvelope)` reconstructs from artifact bodies alone. It has no retained-decision input, so an otherwise complete cause and its descendant become admitted even when a separate retained record blocks the cause. Preserve that decision and the resulting blocked dependency closure in Code; Systems must not implement a second causal algorithm or promote first and delete admitted results afterward.

Extend that existing function with the optional fourth argument `retainedObstructions = []`. Its input is a finite array of exact `{event, obstruction}` records obtained from verified L-S01 retained-obstruction entries by trusted host composition. Event obeys the existing artifact-reference law. Obstruction is the original JSON value, including null, false, numbers, strings, arrays or objects; it is not required to have the current causal-obstruction schema. Validate and snapshot each entry with the existing bounded JSON codec, without invoking accessors or toJSON. Validate the array as an ordinary dense array of own data entries without serializing the whole collection through one artifact envelope. Each entry obeys the existing JSON resource envelope; aggregate retained-source and scan bounds remain the host's L-S03 obligation. Reject malformed input through `causalObstruction("retained-obstruction-invalid", "$.retainedObstructions", "retained obstruction input is invalid")`, without echoing private content. All validation precedes exposure or source reception by a new substrate.

Install the complete retained blocking set before the first promotion pass. Every event named by a retained decision has state blocked, including when its witness body is absent. Missing body does not manufacture a core, artifact, feed membership or admitted event. A later `receive` or `receiveSourceSet` can supply that body but cannot quarantine or admit the blocked reference. A descendant with such a cause is blocked by the existing cause-blocked rule, even if the cause body has not arrived. A retained decision cannot be superseded by ordinary artifacts, later source discovery, source enumeration order or a complete dependency closure. Existing three-argument calls retain their previous behavior.

Keep exact historical decisions separately from derived causal obstructions. Add `retainedObstructions()` returning a deeply immutable array of the exact `{event, obstruction}` snapshots, sorted by ordinal event reference and then ordinal canonical decision text, with only exact canonical duplicates removed. Also include this array under `retainedObstructions` in `snapshot()` so a caller preserving reconstruction inputs does not discard it. Multiple different decisions for one event all survive; no last-file-wins rule applies. `obstruction(event)` for a historically blocked event returns the fixed derived judgment `causalObstruction("retained-block", "$", "a retained journal admission decision blocks this witness", [event])`; the original decision is available through retainedObstructions and is not replaced by that explanation. Existing structurally derived obstruction behavior remains for other events. The snapshot's blocked array includes historically blocked references whose cores are absent, while witnesses lists only actual verified cores.

The host reconstructs afresh from the complete current retained input set for each refreshed logical view, including all retained decisions before computing readiness. Reuse of verified immutable bodies is allowed under L-S05; it does not permit omission of a retained decision. This contract does not add a mutable block/unblock API or admit arbitrary model/remote decisions. Historical affirmative admission evidence contradictory to a retained block is a source conflict to be reported under L-S01; an ordinary retained-witness record is only custody and is not such affirmative evidence. A unique occupied record whose required event is blocked cannot yield successful resolution or a replacement command; preserve the occupancy and return the applicable unavailable diagnostic.

Independent receiving must observe the same blocked cause and descendant across source permutations, exact duplicate and differing retained decisions, an absent blocked body later arriving, unrelated eligible witnesses, a missing unrelated dependency later arriving, and a reconstruction round trip carrying both sourceArtifacts and retainedObstructions. It must preserve falsy historical decisions and refuse malformed retained input without exposing a partial new view. These are pure state effects; accepting the codemod does not accept storage durability, migration, domain authority or the assistant workflow.
